prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core vision
- A “Fair Deal” built on five themes: a stronger green economy; high-quality public services; decisive climate and nature action; a cooperative, outward-looking UK; and a truly fair democracy.
- Restore trust in politics, fix the UK’s relationship with Europe, and put people and communities first.

Economy and business
- Responsible public finances; priority future tax cut by raising the Personal Allowance; reverse bank tax cuts and implement a proper windfall tax on oil and gas.
- Green-led growth: invest in renewables, home insulation and clean industries; national industrial strategy; R&D to 3% of GDP by 2030; reform business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy.
- Skills: replace the apprenticeship levy with a flexible skills levy; £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants; improve careers advice; boost apprenticeships.
- Modern work: create a “dependent contractor” status; overhaul sick pay; living wage review; stronger late payment rules; AI regulation that promotes innovation and accountability.

Health and social care
- Legal right to see a GP within 7 days (24 hours if urgent); 8,000 more GPs; Pharmacy First expansion; fix NHS dentistry access.
- Mental health: hubs for young people everywhere; a professional in every school; regular mental health check-ups.
- Cancer: 100% of patients to start treatment within 62 days; more radiotherapy machines; more cancer nurses.
- Social care: free personal care; a workforce plan, Royal College of Care Workers and a £2/hour Carer’s Minimum Wage; paid carer’s leave and guaranteed respite.

Climate, energy and nature
- Net zero by 2045; 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030; a 10-year home upgrade programme (free insulation/heat pumps for low-income households); rooftop solar push; social tariff; decouple electricity from gas.
- Ban new coal and maintain fracking ban; invest in storage, grid and interconnectors; empower community energy.
- End the sewage scandal: convert water firms to public benefit companies; new tough regulator; sewage tax; binding targets; Clean Air Act; double nature by 2050; 60 million trees/year; protect 30% of land/sea by 2030; deposit return scheme; phase out non-recyclable single-use plastics.

Education and families
- A mental health professional in every school; per-pupil funding rises above inflation; Tutoring Guarantee; fix SEND; restore maintenance grants; return to Erasmus+.
- Early years: extra free hours for disadvantaged 3–4-year-olds; triple Early Years Pupil Premium.
- Parental leave: day‑one rights (incl. self-employed); double Statutory Maternity/Shared Parental Pay to £350/week; extra use‑it‑or‑lose‑it month for fathers; enhanced Child Benefit at age one.
- Free school meals for all children in poverty (aim: all primary pupils).

Welfare, housing and communities
- Scrap the two-child limit and benefit cap; cut UC wait to 5 days; protect triple lock; fair compensation for 1950s-born women; raise and widen Carer’s Allowance.
- Build 380,000 homes/year (150,000 social); ban no‑fault evictions; 3‑year default tenancies; landlord register; abolish leasehold and cap ground rents; end rough sleeping; empower councils on second homes/short‑term lets.
- Multi‑year council funding; nationwide gigabit broadband.

Crime and justice
- Restore community policing; guarantee police attendance and investigation of all burglaries.
- Clear court backlogs; support survivors of violence against women and girls; Online Crime Agency; scrap PCCs; public health approach to youth violence; stronger EU cooperation on crime and data.

Immigration and asylum
- End the Hostile Environment; scrap the Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda plan; safe and legal routes; three‑month decision standard; allow asylum seekers to work after three months.
- Flexible, sector-led work visas; protect EU citizens; reverse family visa threshold hike; expand Youth Mobility.

Rights and democracy
- Defend the Human Rights Act and ECHR; ban conversion practices; scrap anti‑protest laws and live facial recognition; Digital Bill of Rights.
- Proportional representation (STV) for MPs and English councillors; votes at 16; cap donations; enshrine Ministerial Code; reform the Lords; federal UK with stronger devolved powers.

Defence and international
- Increase defence spending towards 2.5% of GDP; reverse Army cuts; maintain nuclear deterrent; tighter arms export controls; parliamentary votes on military action.
- Rebuild ties with Europe via a four‑stage roadmap, aiming for the Single Market and longer‑term EU membership.
- Support Ukraine (including using seized Russian assets); restore aid to 0.7%; immediate ceasefire push and two‑state solution for Israel‑Palestine; robust stance on China and Iran; fund BBC World Service.
